finding.claim: The fence tracking toggles on any line starting with ``` or ~~~, so it ignores the CommonMark rule that a fence closes only on the same character, at least as long as the opener. A ````md fence that shows a ``` example (the usual way to show markdown that contains a fence) flips the state, and the example entry after it is reported as "entry links example.md, which does not exist" (probed - docs/README.md:7). The same happens for ``` inside ~~~. Fix - remember the opener's character and length and close only on a matching line. Non-blocking because the fix is a few mechanical lines plus one test, and the common single-fence case already works.

fixes.change: A fence closes only on the same character at least as long as its opener, an unreadable root index no longer reports every section as unlinked, and _read has a docstring.
Tests for an entry inside a nested fence and for a non-UTF-8 root index giving one finding.
